scope: Read-only diagnosis of the native OfflineAudioContext equal-channel Side cancellation check; no production DSP or test assertions were changed.
findings: Current hidden Side, current visible Side, and baseline visible Side all produce overall RMS 0.014204201553794031, with the only nonzero frames confined to indices 0 through 127.
Their initial 128-frame RMS is 0.0869826150261084 and peak is 0.125. Every subsequent 128-frame chunk is zero; the measured tail after frame 256 and after frame 512 is exactly zero.

Waiting for the actual loudness-worklet promise before OfflineAudioContext.startRendering confirms the worklet exists, but gives the same first-quantum residual in both current and baseline paths. Late asynchronous worklet insertion is therefore not necessary for this residual.

The initial residual is a half-amplitude input sine with opposite signs in L/R. Signs vary across runs/variants. Current visible and baseline visible were bitwise equal in this run; other variants have equal residual magnitude/timing but should not be described as universally bitwise identical.

Baseline hidden Side remains unprocessed for the whole render: RMS 0.17677669361398096 and last nonzero frame 4799. The fixed hidden path has zero output from frame 128 onward, demonstrating restored steady-state Side routing.
No page errors were captured. No claim is made that startup is perfectly silent or that the precise browser/node-level mechanism has been identified.
conclusion: The failing all-frames cancellation assertion exposed an existing graph startup transient. Equivalent baseline-visible and fixed-hidden paths share it. Evidence does not identify a new steady-state graph regression in this patch.
out_of_scope: Further analyser/gain/browser-engine DSP isolation stopped at parent request; no production change made.
